expect.note: CSV rows across each dataset archive, floored near half of the 2026-09 vintage retained under research/epoch/ (data-centers 1496, gpu-clusters 482, chip-components 306, chip-sales 521, companies 236, notable-models 1062, eci ~10000). Epoch republishes a whole vintage, so a dataset that suddenly returns a fraction of its rows is a broken download, not a quiet week. Only the datasets a run actually requests are checked.

The 2026-09 run fetched 18 of 22 quarter files (4 quarters are simply not published yet), kept 569 county rows and built 431 records. Floors sit near half: BLS publishing one fewer quarter is normal, the CSV route going away is not.

The 2026-09 run made 70 county/industry calls, 62 parseable (8 are legitimately suppressed cells), 488 rows, 868 records. Floors near half absorb suppression and a shrinking project map; a dead key or renamed route drops all of them to zero.

Census publishes a biweekly point per series and never withdraws the history, so each of the three metrics held 20 records on 2026-09-09. A floor per metric is what catches the real failure mode here: Census renaming a sector label leaves the file fetchable and that one series empty.

All 13 reviewed domestic filers returned company facts on 2026-09-09 for 424 records. 10 tolerates a couple of transient EDGAR failures; below that the route, the user agent or the ticker map is broken.

From the 2026-09-10 pull (research/eia/eia.json): net-generation 90 rows/90 records, retail-price 518 rows/518 records, capacity-additions 5000 rows and ZERO records, steo 0 rows. The last two are the reason this block exists -- a route that returns rows and produces no record is a parse break, and a route that returns no row at all is a dead query; neither is a quiet week, and both reported ok for as long as this importer has existed.

One call per reviewed query term, all 4 parseable on 2026-09-10. Selecting zero documents is an ordinary quiet week and is not floored; the Federal Register search returning nothing at all for every term over a 120-day lookback is not.

Citation-only: this importer fetches nothing, it registers the reviewed operator sources in research/grid-operators.json (5 on 2026-09-10). The floor guards the reviewed config being emptied, which is the only way this run can silently do nothing.

EIA-930 returned 11234 daily rows for all 4 balancing authorities on 2026-09-10, giving 732 monthly records. Every operator must come back with rows: one respondent code going stale is exactly the failure that otherwise looks like a quiet week.
